'''Patrice Ossona de Mendez''' is a French mathematician specializing in [[topological graph theory]] who works as a researcher at the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] in Paris.<ref name="cv">{{citation|url=http://cams.ehess.fr/pom/Curriculum.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae: Patrice Ossona de Mendez|accessdate=2015-09-20}}.</ref> He is editor-in-chief of the ''[[European Journal of Combinatorics]]'', a position he has held since 2009.<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{citation|url=http://www.journals.elsevier.com/european-journal-of-combinatorics/editorial-board/|title=European Journal of Combinatorics Editorial Board|publisher=Elsevier|accessdate=2015-09-20}}.</ref>

==Education and career==
Ossona de Mendez was born on 13 December 1966 in Paris.<ref name="cv"/> He represented France in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] in 1985, earning a bronze medal there.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=12293|title=Patrice Ossona de Mendez: Individual Ranking|publisher=International Mathematical Olympiad|accessdate=2015-09-20}}.</ref> He studied at the [[École Normale Supérieure]] from 1986 until 1990, and completed his Ph.D. in 1994 from the [[School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences]].<ref name="cv"/> His dissertation, jointly supervised by Rosenstiehl and Hubert de Fraysseix, concerned [[bipolar orientation]]s of graphs.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=93726}}</ref>

He has worked at CNRS since 1995, and earned a [[habilitation]] in 2009 from the [[University of Bordeaux 1]].<ref name="cv"/> 

Together with [[Jaroslav Nešetřil]], he received the 2025 [[Nerode Prize]] for his work on Sparsity for the papers
''Grad and classes with bounded expansion I. Decompositions'', ''Grad and classes with bounded expansion II. Algorithmic aspects'', ''First order properties on nowhere dense structures'',  and ''On nowhere dense graphs''.<ref>{{citation|url=https://eatcs.org/index.php/component/content/article/1-news/3009-eatcs-ipec-nerode-prize-2025|title=EATCS-IPEC Nerode Prize 2025|work=EATCS |publisher=[[European Association for Theoretical Computer Science]]|accessdate=2025-09-26}}.</ref>

==Book==
With [[Jaroslav Nešetřil]], he is the author of the book ''Sparsity: Graphs, Structures, and Algorithms'' ([[Algorithms and Combinatorics]] 28, Springer, 2012), concerning the properties and applications of different types of [[sparse graph]].<ref>Review of ''Sparsity'' by József Balogh, ''[[Mathematical Reviews]]'', {{MR|2920058}}.</ref><ref>Review of ''Sparsity'' by Andre Maximo (October 2012), ''[[ACM Computing Reviews]]'', [http://www.computingreviews.com/review/review_review.cfm?review_id=140602 CR140602].</ref> This book  was included in [[ACM Computing Reviews]]
list of ''Notable Books and Articles of 2012''.<ref>[http://www.computingreviews.com/recommend/bestof/notableitems_2012.cfm ACM Computing Reviews - Notable Computing Books and Articles of 2012], ACM Computing Reviews website. Accessed June 29, 2013</ref>
